cards.text: Here's a Psalm of David, Israel's king, written for the choirmaster according to Jeduthun, one of the musicians chosen to give thanks to the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:41). This one's a song, friend. David starts by telling us where his soul goes to rest.

cards.question: David says his soul finds rest in God and in his own strength.

cards.text: God alone is his rock, his salvation and his fortress. That's not one lock on the door, friend, that's THREE deadbolts.

cards.question: With God as his rock and his fortress, what does David say about himself?

answers.text: He will never lose a battle

cards.text: Then David speaks to the people threatening a man: "How long will you threaten a man?" This didn't start yesterday, friend.

cards.question: David asks the people threatening a man if they'll all throw him down. Throw him down like what?

cards.text: Their whole plan is to cast him down from his lofty perch. And they delight in lies.

cards.question: The people out to cast this man down are two-faced. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they ___.

cards.text: That's the coworker who says "Love it!" in the meeting and then rips it APART in the group chat, friend. Then comes a Selah, and David turns to his own soul and tells it to rest in God alone.

cards.question: David tells his own soul to rest in God alone. What reason does he give?

cards.text: Then that line comes back: God alone is his rock, his salvation and his fortress, and David will not be shaken. And now his salvation and his honor rest on God, his strong rock.

cards.question: David calls out, "Trust in Him at all times, O people…" He also tells them to pour out their hearts before God.

cards.text: Then David says it plain: "God is our refuge." And next, he sizes people up: "Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie."

cards.question: David says lowborn men are a vapor and the exalted are a lie. Weighed on a scale, what happens to them?

cards.text: Put them all together and they're still just a vapor, like the steam off my oven door: there, then GONE. Then David gives a warning: "Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods."

cards.question: David says that if your riches increase, you should set your heart upon them.

cards.text: Then David says God has spoken once, and he has heard it twice. ONCE, friend, and my oven timer has to ding NINE times before I hear it one time.

cards.question: God has spoken once, and David heard it twice. What did David hear?

cards.text: Then David turns and speaks right to God: loving devotion belongs to You, O Lord. Power AND loving devotion, friend, both belong to the same God.

cards.question: David has said not to trust riches, and that lowborn and exalted alike are a vapor. He ends by telling the Lord that He will repay each man according to his ___.
